title: Multiple Dogs and Multiple Courses: Tailwise Training Enrollment Terms
content:
# Enrollments per customer and per dog — Tailwise Training

**Clause 1.** A customer may enroll any number of dogs in Tailwise Training, and one dog may hold several enrollments in different courses. There is no maximum number of enrollments per customer.

**Clause 2.** The dog has no other enrollment in the same course in status enrolled or in progress. It is judged before the enrollment is made, on the company's enrollment records for the dog being enrolled, reading the course and status of each of that dog's existing enrollments.

**Clause 3.** Sessions never pool across enrollments or dogs. Each enrollment holds its own sessions, which can be used only on that enrollment, by that dog.

## The same terms, set out by situation

| Existing enrollment of the same dog | Effect under Clause 2 on a new enrollment in a course |
|---|---|
| Same course, status enrolled (not yet started) | Clause 2 is not met |
| Same course, status in progress | Clause 2 is not met |
| Same course, status completed, withdrawn or expired | Not an enrollment in status enrolled or in progress, so it does not stand against Clause 2 |
| A different course, any status | Not in the same course, so it does not stand against Clause 2; Clause 1 lets one dog hold enrollments in different courses |

An enrollment of a **different dog** of the same customer, in any course, is not an enrollment of this dog and does not bear on Clause 2.

## Points of judgement

**Is there a limit on how many dogs a household can enroll?** No. Clause 1 sets no maximum per customer.

**Can one dog be on two courses at once?** Yes, provided the two are different courses; Clause 2 concerns only another enrollment of the same dog in the same course that is enrolled or in progress.

**Can sessions left on one dog's enrollment be used by another dog, or moved to another enrollment of the same dog?** No. Under Clause 3 sessions never pool across enrollments or dogs.

## Worked example (hypothetical household)

A customer has two dogs. Dog A holds an Adult Basic Training 6-Week Group enrollment that is in progress, and a Private Training 4-Session Pack that is completed. Dog B holds nothing.

- A second Adult Basic Training 6-Week Group enrollment for Dog A: Dog A already has an enrollment in that course in progress, so Clause 2 is not met.
- A new Private Training 4-Session Pack for Dog A: the existing pack is completed, so it does not stand against Clause 2.
- An Adult Basic Training 6-Week Group enrollment for Dog B: Dog B has no enrollment in that course, so Clause 2 is met; Dog A's enrollment belongs to another dog.
- Sessions remaining on Dog A's in-progress course cannot be used by Dog B (Clause 3).
